sentence: On the 10-million-key dataset, Marlin reached a median of 391 thousand operations per second on bulk insert, against 348 for StoneDB and 212 for KVLite.
why: A2 workload A medians are 391 (Marlin), 348 (StoneDB), 212 (KVLite).

sentence: In relative terms, StoneDB's bulk-insert throughput was about 54 percent higher than KVLite's.
why: Arithmetic slip: 348/212 = 1.64, so about 64 percent higher, not 54.

sentence: Marlin's higher write throughput comes from its batched write-ahead log, which groups concurrent writes into a single append.
why: Mechanism/certainty overreach: no profiling, tracing or ablation was run; the README only describes the write path, so causation is untested.

sentence: Marlin's write advantage holds regardless of storage hardware or durability settings.
why: Scope overreach: one machine with NVMe, batched fsync only; per-write fsync and other hardware were not tested.

sentence: KVLite was the fastest store on random point reads, with a median of 455 thousand operations per second.
why: A2 workload B: KVLite 455 [448-463] vs StoneDB 402 and Marlin 417; ranges do not overlap.

sentence: Marlin also serves random reads faster than StoneDB.
why: Statistical overreach: medians 417 vs 402 but ranges [391-426] and [395-410] overlap across 5 runs.

sentence: Under the mixed workload, KVLite's median p99 latency was 4.2 ms, the worst of the three, against 3.1 ms for StoneDB and 2.9 ms for Marlin.
why: Misread cell: A3 gives KVLite p99 as 4.8 ms, not 4.2 (the other two figures are right).

sentence: Marlin's peak resident memory during bulk insert was 5.1 GB, the highest of the three stores.
why: A4: Marlin 5.1, StoneDB 3.4, KVLite 1.9 GB.

sentence: KVLite did not complete the 100M-key bulk insert in any of its three attempts, because the operating system terminated it for exhausting memory.
why: A6 log: all three KVLite runs KILLED by the OOM killer (signal 9).

sentence: Because the 100M-key comparison used only three runs per store, the gap between Marlin's 312 and StoneDB's 301 thousand operations per second should be treated as unresolved.
why: Appropriately hedged: A6 medians 312 vs 301 from 3 runs with overlapping ranges [288-330] and [295-306].

sentence: StoneDB sustains its mixed-workload throughput over long-running operation.
why: Temporal overreach: longest run was 6 minutes (A1, A5 show steady per-minute figures over 5 minutes); no soak or multi-hour test.

sentence: Marlin's own documentation presents it as the right engine for write-intensive systems generally.
why: Authority/source overreach: README says only 'designed for write-intensive workloads whose reads mostly touch recently written keys' (conditional); the benchmark used uniform random reads.

sentence: The journal contains 212 dated entries, of which 71 concern the weather.
why: E2 and E3 both total 212; weather is 71.

sentence: Wray kept a continuous day-by-day record of the winter.
why: Completeness overreach: 212 entries over 716 days, none from 12 Dec 1741 to 26 Jan 1742 (missing folios 31-34), and some entries written up later.

sentence: The 1911 editor judged that several entries were written up some weeks after the dates they carry.
why: Q7 (Ed. p. xv) says exactly this.

sentence: Wray records wheat at 5 shillings a bushel in November 1741 and at 9 shillings in March 1742.
why: E4: Nov 1741 fol. 12v = 5s; Mar 1742 fol. 40r = 9s.

sentence: He also notes that Pell's mill stood idle for eleven weeks while its wheel was held fast in the ice, so the parish sent its grain to Aldby for grinding.
why: Q4 (fol. 39v) states this.

sentence: The surviving folios give a single figure for money raised for poor relief: £11 4s from a rate of fourpence in the pound.
why: Q3 and E5(c): £11 4s on fol. 38v is the only relief sum in the surviving folios.

sentence: The parish register shows 52 burials in 1742, which is 23 more than in 1741.
why: Arithmetic slip: E5(a) gives 52 in 1742 and 33 in 1741, a difference of 19.

sentence: Of the 29 death entries in the journal, Wray names a fever as the cause in seven.
why: Miscount: E5(b) gives fever named in 5 of the 29 entries, not 7.

sentence: The frost alone accounts for the rise in burials in 1742.
why: Causal-exclusivity overreach: cold is named in only 6 of 29 death entries, a fever in 5 (Q6), and 18 give no cause.

sentence: Wray's burial entries have been checked against the parish register and found accurate.
why: Partial-verification overreach: the editor checked only 9 of Wray's 29 burial notices and did not check the rest (Q8).

sentence: Wray states that the vicar kept the tithe barn locked against the poor.
why: Hearsay presented as assertion: Q5 reports 'it is said by some', Wray disclaims having seen it, and the vicar says the barn is empty.

sentence: The journal gives a representative picture of how rural parishes in the county fared that winter.
why: Representativeness overreach: one clerk, one parish, and the edition contains no comparative material (E1).

sentence: Of 112 nurses screened, 64 were randomized, 32 to each arm.
why: T2: 112 screened, 64 randomized, 32 per arm.

sentence: Of the 48 nurses who were screened but not randomized, most (31) declined to take part.
why: Misread cell: T2 shows 31 were ineligible and 17 declined.

sentence: Eight-week retention was 84.4% in the app arm (27 of 32) and 90.6% in the control arm (29 of 32).
Across both arms, 56 of 64 participants (85.9%) completed the week 8 assessment.
why: Arithmetic slip: 56/64 = 87.5% (T2), not 85.9%.

sentence: Among completers, the Insomnia Severity Index fell by 5.3 points in the app arm and 1.4 points in the control arm, a between-group difference of 3.9 points (95% CI 1.9 to 5.9).
why: T4 completers row: -5.3 vs -1.4, difference -3.9 (-5.9 to -1.9).

sentence: The reduction in insomnia severity persisted after the program ended.
why: Temporal overreach: only baseline and week 8 were assessed; no follow-up after the program ended was planned (T1, T7 s6.3).

sentence: The sleep-restriction module is what drove the improvement.
why: Mechanism/attribution overreach: components were delivered together and not tested individually (T7 s3.1), with a no-contact waitlist comparator.

sentence: The sleep-diary estimate of total sleep time was imprecise: the app arm's 16-minute advantage came with a confidence interval running from a 9-minute loss to a 41-minute gain.
why: Appropriately hedged: T4 sleep-diary row is +16 min (-9 to +41), p = 0.21.

sentence: Engagement with the program was high.
why: Strength overreach: T5 shows a median of 5 of 8 modules, only 11 of 32 completing all 8, and 2 completing none.

sentence: No serious adverse events were reported, and the two mild events, both transient worsening of sleep in the first week, occurred in the app arm.
why: T6: 0 serious events in either arm; 2 mild events, both in the app arm.

sentence: These data show the program is safe for night-shift nurses.
why: Certainty overreach: 32 exposed participants over 8 weeks, free-text AE collection that differed by arm, and the protocol states the study is not powered for safety.

sentence: The findings apply to shift workers generally.
why: Population-scope overreach: only nurses with at least 3 night shifts a week at one teaching hospital (T1, T3).

sentence: All four specimens tested at 3.0 kN reached the 2,000,000-cycle runout, and dye-penetrant inspection found no cracks in any of them.
why: F3 and the F5 log: F3-01 to F3-04 runout, DPI no indications.

sentence: Below 3.0 kN the bracket has an effectively infinite fatigue life.
why: Extrapolation overreach: nothing was tested below 3.0 kN, runouts were stopped at 2,000,000 cycles, and n = 4 at 3.0 kN.

sentence: No specimens were tested at 3.5 kN, the level named in the requirement, so compliance at that load is not directly demonstrated.
why: Appropriately hedged: F3 note says no specimen was tested at 3.5 kN; levels were 3.0, 4.0 and 5.0 kN.

sentence: One of the four specimens reached the runout and the other three failed, the shortest at 1,138,000 cycles.
why: Misread cell: F3 shows the shortest 4.0 kN life as F4-04 at 1,238,000 cycles.

sentence: At 4.0 kN the bracket has a 75 percent chance of failing before two million cycles.
why: Precision overreach: 3 of 4 specimens failed, one result is flagged INTERRUPTED, and no statistical analysis or interval was done.

sentence: At 5.0 kN all four specimens failed, at between 366,000 and 508,000 cycles.
The mean life at 5.0 kN was about 483,000 cycles.
why: Arithmetic slip: the four lives sum to 1,733,000, so the mean is about 433,000.

sentence: Seven of the eight static specimens showed a permanent set of 0.05 mm or less after loading to 12 kN.
why: F4: S01 to S07 read 0.02 to 0.05 mm; only S08 is above.

sentence: Specimen S08 exceeded the 0.10 mm acceptance limit, with a permanent set of 0.21 mm.
why: F4 and the log: S08 = 0.21 mm, re-read 0.21 mm.

sentence: The excess set in S08 is explained by its coming from a different material lot.
why: Causal overreach: S08 is the only lot B specimen, with no certificate on file and no sectioning, hardness or tensile tests, so cause is undetermined.

sentence: The bracket's performance carries over to the full range of service temperatures.
why: Conditions overreach: all tests at 20.1-22.6 C, while REQ-EN-003 spans -30 C to +50 C.

sentence: The fatigue programme was run in accordance with ASTM E466.
why: Standard-compliance overreach: TP-221 says only 'adapted from ASTM E466' and lists deviations (4 specimens per level against a target of 6, no alignment verification).
